subject: Urgent: FastRetail elevated 5xx/429 + retry amplification
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fastretail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Gomez <tina@cloudproc.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx/429 rate observed, huge retry storms — urgent

Team,

We started seeing a significant increase in 5xx and 429 responses for our checkout traffic around 08:45 PST this morning. Token-level error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~8% and overall latency tail moved from p95 300ms to p95 2.6s. Our integrator is receiving repeated timeouts which triggers client retries — we are seeing clear amplification. This is impacting checkout throughput and customers are abandoning carts.

Attached: request-trace-20261217.zip (contains sampled request traces and client-side retry logs).

Can you please confirm receipt and share immediate mitigations you can apply? We need an ETA for a fix and a short-term mitigation (circuit-breaker, stricter client-side retry guidance, rate limit?) so we can stabilize customer experience.

Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fastretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 09:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate observed, huge retry storms — urgent

Alex — thanks for the quick flag and for the traces. We see the same signals in our telemetry. I'm standing up an incident working group now and will coordinate with you directly. Immediate plan (15m cadence updates):

- Short-term: enable tenant-level concurrency cap and a 50ms early-fail threshold on long-poll requests to cut amplification.
- Mid-term (1–3 hrs): deploy a config change that enforces fail-fast for known retrying clients and pin FastRetail traffic to an isolated serving pool where possible.
- Communication: Sean will send a customer-facing status update within 30 minutes.

I've CC'd Dev (eng) and Marcus (ops) to own the fixes. We'll also produce a MAP (mutual action plan) doc and share after our first update.

Attachment: map-fastretail-v1.docx (draft mutual action plan).

—Priya

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: FastRetail incident — immediate action items (do not forward)

Confirming ownership of containment. Quick technical notes from initial triage:

- Root cause hypothesis: a recent default change to the client retry header (client_max_retries=6) combined with longer p50 backend processing on a minority of model variants produced a retry amplification loop. The handler that holds KV-cache locks for prefix contexts is causing requests to queue, which produces latency tail and more retries.

Immediate actions I will perform (ETA 45m):
1) Deploy a config toggle to enforce tenant-level concurrency limit = 50 for FastRetail and enable a short-circuit response (503 + Retry-After) to encourage backoff.
2) Add a server-side fail-fast for requests with elapsed > 900ms to avoid holding cache locks.
3) Roll a targeted kernel patch to reduce lock contention for KV cache (low risk, quick rollback).

I attached the minimal patch that toggles the fail-fast path and the config toggle: patch-fix-timeout.diff (text). I'll post progress here.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate observed, huge retry storms — urgent

Alex — quick status update for customers:

What happened: we observed an elevated 5xx/429 rate affecting FastRetail starting ~08:45 PST; customer-side retries amplified the impact.
What we did: applied a tenant-level concurrency cap and enabled a short-circuit fail-fast path to reduce amplification. We also rolled a low-risk patch to reduce KV cache lock contention.
Next steps:
- We are continuing to monitor; p95 latency for FastRetail has reduced from ~2.6s to ~420ms after the containment steps.
- Eng will run a follow-up to remove the root cause and publish a full postmortem with actions (alerting, runbook updates, SLO tuning, capacity reservation).

We will schedule a 1:1 debrief tomorrow to review longer-term mitigations.

Sean Gallagher
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rate observed, huge retry storms — urgent

Alex — follow-up and actions (summary):

Summary: Containment succeeded and we reduced customer-visible errors. Root cause: client retry defaults + rare backend tail causing lock contention and multi-request queuing which amplified retries.

Immediate actions taken (Dec 17):
- Tenant concurrency cap + short-circuit fail-fast deployed (reduced amplification).
- Low-risk kernel/lock patch rolled to reduce KV cache contention.
- Increased trace sampling for your tenant; we ingested the traces you shared.

Planned follow-ups (timeline):
- Within 48 hrs: calibrate SLOs and alert thresholds for FastRetail-specific traffic; add per-tenant 5xx/429 early-warning alerts.
- 1 week: update runbook with explicit retry-amplification mitigation steps and automated playbook to pin serving pool.
- 2–3 weeks: capacity plan — evaluate reserved pool for FastRetail at target Q4 traffic, recommend Dedicated pool or burst SLA.
- Postmortem: full RCA doc and action tracker will be shared by next Wednesday (Dec 23).

If you prefer, we can set a call to walk through the postmortem and planned capacity options. Thank you again for the traces — they sped up diagnosis.

Best,
